authorship: Hand-authored scheduler witnesses over docs/X1_TRANSPORT_CONTRACT.md section 5. Expected observations describe the injected fake engine/clock logs; no production scheduler exists or was consulted.

cases.title: One schedule per event across overlapping ticks

expected.law: Beat 0 enters the first horizon [0, 0.1]; beats 1 and 2 map to 0.5 s and 1.0 s and stay outside every listed horizon. Repeated ticks over an unchanged horizon must not reissue the beat-0 batch; the cursor advances exactly once.

cases.title: Ascending startTick order within one horizon

expected.law: At 240 BPM beats 0, 1/4, and 3/8 map to 0, 0.0625, and 0.09375 seconds, all inside one 0.1 s horizon, and must be issued in ascending exact startTick order in one tick. Beat 1/2 (0.125 s) would fall outside the horizon.

cases.title: Stale tick after generation boundary schedules nothing
cases.scenario: A tick captured generation G, then Stop crossed to G+1 before the tick body ran.

expected.law: A callback whose captured generation is no longer current increments staleCallbacksIgnored and performs no engine call, cursor move, or notification.

cases.title: Loop wrap crosses one loop-wrap generation boundary and re-anchors

expected.law: Reaching the loop end retires the outgoing generation, increments it once, re-anchors the epoch at the loop start's exact beat, and never touches the persistent graph.

cases.title: Attack lead never exceeds the X0 admission window

expected.law: With the maximum legal lookahead, every issued startTimeSeconds is at most currentTime + 0.2, leaving the frozen 0.05 s margin under X0's 0.25 s admission ceiling; transport.engine_refusal for lateness is unreachable by construction.

cases.title: Instrument change rewinds and reschedules only the unattacked horizon
cases.scenario: Events A (sounding), B and C (scheduled, start in the future) exist when set-instrument is admitted.

expected.law: B and C are retired with sources stopped at or before their starts, the cursor rewinds over exactly B and C, and both are reissued with the new recipe at their original exact times. A keeps its recipe.

cases.title: Count-in prepends exactly one bar of clicks

expected.law: Four clicks at beats -4..-1 precede beat zero; the downbeat click is accented; plan events shift by exactly one bar of transport time while plan beats stay untouched.

cases.title: Metronome clicks on integer beats while playing

expected.law: One click per integer beat, accent on each bar's downbeat, generated inside the same lookahead horizon discipline as plan events and counted separately from eventsScheduled.

cases.title: Click IDs cannot collide with document events

expected.law: Every generated click event ID starts with the reserved prefix. The prefix contains a colon, which the document event grammar never produces, so a click can never retire or retrigger a document event's voices.

cases.title: Scheduler stops ticking when exhausted without a loop

expected.law: With the cursor exhausted and no loop, the control timer is cleared; natural-end handling owns the remaining tail deadline. An idle transport performs zero engine calls.

cases.title: Empty plan publishes an immediate natural end

expected.law: A zero-event plan (empty chart) plays as silence of the plan's exact total beats; a zero-beat plan ends immediately at ready with the playhead at startBeat. Whole-chart silence caused by scheduling defects is the L-RUNTIME-01 regression; silence here must come only from an exactly empty timeline.

cases.title: Tempo change maps the exact beat across epochs
cases.scenario: Playing at 120 BPM, playhead at exact beat 3/2; set-tempo binding at 60 BPM is admitted.

expected.law: The exact rational playhead beat carries into the new epoch anchor unchanged; only seconds-per-beat changes. Sounding voices decay naturally; not-yet-attacked horizon voices are retired and rescheduled at new-tempo seconds.
No animation-frame callback appears in the platform port; the injected timer port is the only control-thread ticker, and disabling every animation frame changes no scheduling observation.

cases.title: Suspended clock freezes musical time
cases.scenario: The audio clock reports the same currentTimeSeconds across three ticks during a platform suspension.

expected.law: A non-advancing audio clock advances no beats and schedules nothing new; wall time is irrelevant. Musical time resumes only when the audio clock resumes.
